h1: Beer festivals in India and how to make a weekend of one
title: Beer Festivals in India: Make a Weekend | Craft Beer School
desc: How to turn an Indian beer festival into a weekend: when festivals happen, how to plan travel and stay, what to taste and how to stay safe.
teaser: A beer festival is one day. With a little planning, it can be the best weekend of your season.
standfirst: India now hosts beer festivals in several cities, most of them in the cooler months. Here is how to turn one into a relaxed weekend of tasting, food and brewery visits.
sections:
Indian beer festivals tend to cluster in the cooler months, from around October to February, when outdoor events are comfortable. Cities with strong brewpub scenes, such as Bengaluru, Pune, Mumbai, Goa and the Delhi NCR, host many of them. Some are large ticketed events with dozens of breweries. Others are smaller gatherings run by a single brewpub or a group of local brewers.

Dates and line-ups change every year. Follow brewpubs and brewers you like on social media; they usually announce festival appearances weeks ahead. Always check the organiser's own page for the date, venue, entry age and what the ticket includes.
What the ticket usually gets you

Many festivals sell entry with a set number of tasting tokens or a tasting glass. Small pours of 100 to 150 ml are common. That is the point: you can taste ten beers from ten breweries for less alcohol than you might think, as long as you count.

Read the ticket details. Some include food. Some charge extra for tokens. Some sell beer only by the glass. Knowing in advance stops you from overspending at the gate.
Why the cooler months suit festivals

Indian summers are hard on beer and on people. Beer warms quickly in the glass outdoors, which changes how it tastes and makes it feel heavier. A wheat beer served at 6 °C can be well above 15 °C within minutes in afternoon sun. Brewers also struggle to keep kegs cold at an outdoor stall in 35 °C heat, so the beer you taste may not be at its best.

The cooler months fix most of that. Beer stays cold longer, crowds are more comfortable and you are less likely to get dehydrated. That is one reason most organisers pick the months after the monsoon.

If you do go to a summer or indoor event, take small pours and drink them quickly while they are cold. Our guide to a Belgian wit in Pune is a reminder that lighter, refreshing styles are made for warm days.

If the festival is in another city, make the trip worth it:

  • Friday: travel in, check into a hotel close to the venue and have an early dinner.
  • Saturday: the festival. Go early to beat the queues. Leave before the crush at closing.
  • Sunday: a slow brunch and a visit to one brewpub you discovered at the festival.

Staying within walking distance of the venue or close to a metro station solves the hardest problem of the weekend: getting back safely.

Indian beer festivals usually have strong food stalls. Eat early and keep eating. Spicy food changes how beer tastes. Chilli heat makes bitterness feel sharper and alcohol feel hotter, so malty, wheat or lighter beers often sit better with spicy dishes than big bitter IPAs. Our guide to beer and spicy food explains why.

Try pairing the same beer with two different dishes. It is one of the best ways to learn how beer and food work together.
Stay safe and look after each other

Carry government photo ID. The legal drinking age varies by state, from 18 to 25. Organisers check it at the gate. Drink water between tasters. Set a limit before you arrive.

Never drive after a festival. Book a cab, take the metro or walk back to your hotel. If you are going alone, share your location with a friend. Look out for anyone in your group who has had too much and get them water, food and a ride home.
Make the most of the brewers

A festival brings brewers out from behind their tanks. Ask them about the beer: what malt and hops they used, why they chose that yeast, what they are brewing next. Most enjoy the questions. You will leave with a list of brewpubs to visit and beers to look out for.

Keep notes. Brewery, beer, style and three words for each. Our guide to where to drink a hefeweizen in Bengaluru is one example of how far a good note can lead.

Pick a theme for the day: every wheat beer, every stout, or one beer from each brewery you have never tried. Comparing like with like teaches you far more than wandering stall to stall.

Most people find they can tell beers apart but cannot say why. Learning a tasting vocabulary is what turns a fun day into a skill you keep.

Your first step: follow five Indian brewpubs you like on social media this week so you hear about the next festival in your city as soon as it is announced.
faqs: When are beer festivals held in India?
Most cluster in the cooler months, from around October to February. Dates change every year, so check the organiser's page.
What is included in a beer festival ticket?
It varies. Many include entry plus tasting tokens or a glass. Some include food. Read the ticket details before you buy.
Do I need ID at an Indian beer festival?
Yes. The legal drinking age varies by state and organisers check it at the gate, so carry a government photo ID.
